input.sourceText: When I consider the memories associated with the last day at our old address, there is one object that for me seemed to assume a greater significance than the other things I was engaged in packing. It was a postcard with a sketch of our street on the front. I'd put it in a box with the rest of my papers. At the door, I realised I was going to pass the postbox for the last time. I went back for the card and wrote our new address on it. Until then, I had thought I'd keep it. I posted it to myself on the way to the bus. Two days later it was in the hall at the new place, face down on the mat.
input.requirements: Keep the change of mind in the story and the quiet ending.

When I think about the occasion on which I took my first bicycle ride to work, the part that continues to stand out to me is a conversation at the traffic light. I had started down the wrong street and stopped at the light. Another rider asked whether I was looking for the riverside path. I said I was, and she pointed to the entrance behind the bakery.

I used that entrance again the next day. This time I got to work without taking a wrong turn.

Revision

I took the same entrance the next day and got to work without a wrong turn.

Meaning check
The opening puts the reader at the traffic light, while the memory still belongs to the narrator. It preserves the wrong turn, the rider's question and directions, the entrance behind the bakery, and the following day's ride. The new order uses only details given by the narrator.

polishedText:
On the last day at our old address, I was packing when one object came to seem more significant than the rest: a postcard with a sketch of our street on the front. I put it in a box with my other papers.

At the door, I realised I was going to pass the postbox for the last time. I went back for the card and wrote our new address on it. Until then, I had thought I'd keep it. I posted it to myself on the way to the bus.

Two days later it was in the hall at the new place, face down on the mat.
